claims.explanation: NVP-AUY922 is a potent HSP90 inhibitor whose selectivity is largely driven by dependence on HSP90 client proteins, particularly mutated/activated kinases such as BRAF, EGFR, ERBB2, MET, and PIK3CA/AKT signaling, which are degraded upon HSP90 inhibition. Lines with these oncogenic drivers (e.g., BRAF-mutant melanoma, EGFR-mutant lung, MET-amplified gastric, PIK3CA-mutant breast/ovarian) are sensitized, while lines lacking such clients or with protective features like high HSP70/HSPA1A expression or NFE2L2/KEAP1 mutations are less affected.

features.basis: BRAF is an HSP90 client; mutant BRAF is degraded by HSP90 inhibition, and BRAF-mutant lines (WM793, 8305C, HEC265) are among the most killed
Mutant EGFR is an HSP90 client; EGFR-mutant lines (NCIH1650, KYSE70, KYSE270) are selectively killed
ERBB2 (HER2) is a classic HSP90 client; high expression predicts sensitivity to HSP90 inhibitors
MET is an HSP90 client; MET-mutant/amplified lines (HGC27, 8305C) are among the most killed
PIK3CA-mutant lines (SNU840, KYSE70, HCC1954, HGC27) are enriched among sensitive lines, consistent with HSP90-dependent PI3K/AKT signaling
High HSP70 (HSPA1A) expression compensates for HSP90 inhibition and is associated with resistance
NFE2L2/KEAP1 mutations are enriched in resistant lines (SNUC5, LUDLU1, KYSE520), possibly via antioxidant response
TP53 mutations are common in both sensitive and resistant lines, but many sensitive lines are TP53-mutant; weak evidence
NRAS is an HSP90 client; NRAS-mutant lines (IPC298, SW1088) are among the most killed
KRAS is an HSP90 client; KRAS-mutant lines (NCIH1792, OV7, PATU8988S) are among the most killed
CDKN2A mutations appear in several resistant lines (YD10B, SNU1214, KELLY, MHHES1), but also in sensitive lines; weak evidence
ARID1A mutations appear in several sensitive lines (KYSE70, EFE184, HEC265, SW1088), but mechanism unclear; weak evidence
